svg.title: GeoMesh.py: the recorded calls SALOME replays, from Room to create_mesh, and the named face groups (wall, objects, inlet, outlet) that become OpenFOAM patches
svg.text: GeoMesh.py — builds the room, its patches and the mesh inside SALOME
It runs in SALOME's embedded Python, not yours: SALOME replays machine_script.py against these same-named classes.
then each recorded line, in order
The fluid volume: a dx × dy × dz box with Y pointing up.
Also creates the Salome_Env (geometry builder, axes) on first use.
One solid each, placed at (x, z). name= is required.
Diffusers hang from the ceiling: their y is the drop below it.
Splits a circle of radius d out of the ceiling (y = dy) or floor (y = 0).
Call before add(): these small faces become the outlet.
Cuts every object out of the room volume, then create_faces_groups()
sorts the remaining faces into named groups: the patches on the right.
Local refinement volumes around a person or a diffuser jet.
NETGEN 1D-2D surface + 3D tetrahedra, with a surface size and viscous
layers per patch type (table, right). Compute(), then ExportUNV.
Flags elements past the threshold → <metric>_df.csv, plus a summary .txt.
What step 4 produces: named face groups
side view (x–y), not to scale; each group becomes an OpenFOAM patch
▦ = 5 viscous (boundary) layers are also grown on that patch
Keep the two copies in sync
SALOME imports its own copy of GeoMesh.py from its site-packages.
Edit src/GeoMesh.py → copy it there again, or SALOME runs the old one.
docs/installation.md shows where that folder is.
